root_cause.text: The ksmbd subsystem contains a timing side-channel vulnerability because it uses the non-constant-time `memcmp()` function to verify authentication MACs and signatures.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `memcmp()` with `crypto_memneq()` in `fs/smb/server/auth.c` and `fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c`, and the CVE description explicitly mandates constant-time MAC comparisons to prevent timing attacks.

relevance_review.reason: The group addresses build configuration issues (missing dependencies and headers) rather than the security logic flaw. The vulnerability stems from using a non-constant-time memcmp() function, which requires code logic changes to fix, not merely build system adjustments.

The code changes directly address the root cause by replacing the non-constant-time memcmp() function with the constant-time crypto_memneq() function in authentication MAC and signature verification contexts, which eliminates the timing side-channel vulnerability described.

vuln_statements.explanation: This memcmp() call in the authentication MAC verification path uses non-constant-time comparison, enabling timing side-channel attacks. An attacker can measure response time differences to gradually learn valid authentication tokens. The auth.c file has the highest relevance (0.85) and contains the critical authentication verification logic where this vulnerability manifests.

This memcmp() call in SMB2 signature verification also uses non-constant-time comparison. The smb2pdu.c file handles SMB3 signing key operations and signature verification (snippet shows signing_key handling and memcpy for signature). Using memcmp() instead of constant-time comparison functions like crypto_memneq() allows timing-based attacks on signature validation.
